messages.content: Drills leave the tool library and don't return. I need one decision a volunteer can run on Saturday.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=brainstorm|construct=brainstorm|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
The logician wants the smallest mechanism that changes the cost. The volunteer wants something they can explain at the door. The critic notes that a card hold fails if people pay cash. Those agree on a deposit, cash or card, released when the drill comes back. A reminder and a wall of shame don't survive the critic. The winning vector is the deposit.
</think>

[SWARM VERDICT]
Take a deposit on Saturday, cash or card, and give it back with the drill. The objection that survived is that some people have no card, so cash has to count. A reminder doesn't change anything.
Friday's demo has slipped three times. Pick a rule for this Friday only.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=brainstorm|construct=brainstorm|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
One angle is a louder calendar. It doesn't change the size of the promise. Another is cutting the demo to a single clickable path and deleting the rest from the invite. A third is cancelling. Cancelling teaches nothing and the team still has no demo. The clickable path is what a person can finish, and the critic's objection, that the rest of the work becomes invisible, is handled by not putting it on Friday's invite rather than by pretending it doesn't exist.
</think>

[SWARM VERDICT]
Friday shows one path a person can click. Everything else comes off the invite. The objection that the other work vanishes is met by not calling it Friday's demo, not by cancelling.
Name the library. Three directions, one I'd paint on the glass.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=brainstorm|construct=brainstorm|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
A plain verb, a concrete noun, and a rule. Borrowed. The Drill Next Door. Bring It Back. The painter wants something readable from the street. The critic wants the failure mode of the place in the name. Bring It Back is the one both accept. The other two are fine and they don't say the hard part.
</think>

[SWARM VERDICT]
Paint Bring It Back. Borrowed and The Drill Next Door are real names and they don't tell a stranger the rule.
New hire, second day, has to learn the deploy. Pick the exercise.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=brainstorm|construct=brainstorm|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Reading the doc leaves their hands off it. Shadowing a real deploy has a blast radius. A no-op deploy they roll back, with someone watching, teaches the command while nothing is at stake. That's the one. The doc becomes homework after they have typed the command.
</think>

[SWARM VERDICT]
They roll back a no-op deploy while you watch. Reading and shadowing don't put the command in their hands while it's still harmless.
